MCF-7 human mammary carcinoma cell cytoskeletons formed in three-dimensional cellular structures floating in a medium and in monolayers on a plastic substratum are different in their buoyant density, polypeptide composition, and ultrastructural appearance.
the cytoskeletal structure of human mammary carcinoma cell MCF-7 grown as monolayer on plastic substratum is different from that of the same cell grown as cellular structures within collagen gel.
the cytoskeletal network of MCF- 7 cells forming the morphologically developing structures within collagen gelt is coarser and denser than that of the cells growing as monolayers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cytoskeletons of MCF- 7 cells grown on collagen gels and the morphologically developing MCF-7 cellular structures within collagen matrices.
the morphological and biochemical changes in human mammary tumor cells during the formation of three-dimensional cellular structures,
the morphological and biochemical characterization of the cytoskeleton during the formation of cellular structures in three dimensions by human mammary carcinoma cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cytoskeletal structure of the morphologically developing MCF-7 cell is more similar to that of the monodispersed MCF-7 spheroids than that of the MCF-7 monolayer on a plastic substratum, and the cytoskeletal network of the developing cell has a coarser structure and is more resistant to Triton than that of the spheroidal cells.

the cytoskeletal structure of the cells forming three-dimensional structures within collagen gell differs significantly from those of the cells grown as mononlayers on plastic substrata, in terms of both the polypeptide composition and the cytoskeletal network.

the cytoskeletal structure of MCF- 7 cells grown as three-dimensional cellular structures in type I collagen gell differs from that of the monlayered cells in the buoyant density, polypeptide composition, and cytoskeletal network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytoskeletal organization in MCF-7 mammary carcinoma cells is altered during their morphological development from the monolayer to the three-dimensional cellular structure within collagen gels.

the cytoskeletal organization of the cells in the three-dimensional cellular structure within the collagen gel differs from that of the cells on plastic substratum, and the cytoskeleton is related to the morphological development of the cells.

the cytoskeletal structure of the morphologically developing MCF-7 human mammary carcinoma cell is more similar to that of fibroblasts, and that it is more closely related to the cytoskeleton in the morphologically nondeveloping MCF-7 mammary carcinoma cells than to the cytoskeletal network in the fibroblast-like monolayered MCF-7 cell on the plastic substratum.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cytoskeletal structure of MCF- 7 cells grown as a monolayer on plastic substratum is different from that of the cells forming the three- dimensional cellular structures within type I collagen gela.

the cytoskeletal network of MCF- 7 cells grown as a monolayer on plastic substratum has a finer cytoskeleton than that of the cells grown as cellular structures within collagen gel, and that the cytoskelton of the cells forming the cellular structures within collagen is lacking in two distinct polypeptide components.
the cytoskeletal organization is different in the three-dimensional structures formed by MCF-7 cell in collagen gels and the two-dimensional structures formed by the same cells on plastic substrata.
